text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New Bloc boss has rocky start: Duceppe finds pitfalls lurking in his own ranks and across the floor.
- British election called for May 1: Major confident despite polls.
- Yeltsin recruits top young reformer: Russia on greater pro-Western course.
- Foes lie in wait for Charest: Conservatives' credibility, record are prime targets for rival parties.
- Minor miscreants avoid court system's web: New programs tailor punishment to the offence and free up courts.
- Mutual fund sales set record: Canadians pumped C$10 billion in new money into funds last month, eclipsing 1994 mark.
- Eaton's hires bankers to sell or merge chain: Stores to be closed 6 months sooner.
- Quebec securities regulator to become self-funding unit: Bay Street expected to press for similar changes in Ontario.
- Mining expert warns against corruption: Urges World Bank to tie loans to record.
- Eaton's goes up for sale: Store closings brought forward by as much as six months and two top investment firms to help line up buyers for the company.
- Ottawa to curb immigrant investor program.
